provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Introduction to Digital Entrepreneurship
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define digital entrepreneurship
The students should be able to list three skills needed for digital entrepreneurship
The students should be able to identify two opportunities in digital entrepreneurship

Introduction:
Today we will learn about digital entrepreneurship. We have learned about computers and the internet before.

Content:
Digital entrepreneurship means using technology to start and run a business. It is important because it helps create jobs and makes business easier. Skills needed include computer knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving. Opportunities include selling goods online, providing digital services, and creating apps. For example, a young Nigerian can sell clothes on Instagram or create a website for local market traders.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to brainstorm three digital business ideas that could work in Nigeria.

Evaluation questions:
What is digital entrepreneurship?
Name two skills needed for digital entrepreneurship.
Give one example of digital entrepreneurship in Nigeria.

Summary:
Digital entrepreneurship uses technology to create businesses and solve problems.

topics.title: Internet Communication and Collaboration Em
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain how email works
The students should be able to list three collaboration tools
The students should be able to identify the benefits of video calls

Introduction:
We have learned about the internet before. Today we will learn how we use it to communicate and work together.

Content:
Email is electronic mail that lets people send messages over the internet. Video calls allow people to see and hear each other in real time, like when family members in different cities talk. Cloud tools like Google Docs let people work on the same document at the same time. These tools help Nigerians work together even when far apart, like when students in different schools work on a project.

Class activity:
Students will practice sending emails and creating a shared document with a partner.

Evaluation questions:
What is email?
Name two collaboration tools.
How can video calls help people in Nigeria?

Summary:
Internet tools help people communicate and work together from different places.

topics.title: Social Media for Education and Business
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain responsible use of social media
The students should be able to describe how to build a personal brand
The students should be able to list two ways to promote a business on social media

Introduction:
We use social media every day. Today we will learn how to use it wisely for school and for business.

Content:
Responsible use means being careful what you post and how you treat others online. Building a brand means creating a good image for yourself or your business. For education, students can follow accounts that teach subjects like Mathematics. For business, sellers can use Instagram to show products and Facebook to reach customers. A local food seller in Lagos can use WhatsApp to take orders and show food pictures.

Class activity:
Students will create a simple social media profile for a fictional Nigerian business.

Evaluation questions:
What does responsible use of social media mean?
How can social media help with learning?
Name one way to promote a business on social media.

Summary:
Social media can help with learning and business if used properly.

topics.title: Digital Marketing Basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define digital marketing
The students should be able to list two channels of digital marketing
The students should be able to explain how to advertise safely online

Introduction:
We have learned about social media for business. Today we will learn how to market products using digital tools.

Content:
Digital marketing means promoting products or services using the internet. Channels include social media, email, and websites. For example, a shoe seller in Abuja can use Instagram to show new shoes. To advertise safely, businesses should not lie about products, should protect customer information, and should respect privacy. A good practice is to get permission before sending marketing emails.

Class activity:
Students will design a simple digital ad for a common Nigerian product.

Evaluation questions:
What is digital marketing?
Name two channels of digital marketing.
Why is it important to advertise safely online?

Summary:
Digital marketing helps businesses reach customers using internet tools.

topics.title: MID-TERM TEST
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of digital entrepreneurship
The students should be able to show understanding of internet communication tools
The students should be able to explain social media for business
The students should be able to describe digital marketing basics

Introduction:
Today we will have our test to see what we have learned so far this term.

Content:
This test will cover digital entrepreneurship, internet communication, social media for business, and digital marketing. Students will answer questions about these topics. The test will check if students remember the main ideas and can apply them.

Class activity:
Students will complete a written test covering weeks 1-4.

Evaluation questions:
The test will have multiple choice and short answer questions about the topics covered.

Summary:
This test will help teachers know what students have learned so far.

topics.title: Cyber Ethics and Netiquette
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define cyber ethics
The students should be able to list three rules of good netiquette
The students should be able to identify respectful online behavior

Introduction:
We have learned how to use the internet for business. Today we will learn how to behave properly online.

Content:
Cyber ethics means rules for good behavior on the internet. Netiquette is internet etiquette, or good manners online. Rules include being polite in messages, not sharing others' private information, and not spreading fake news. For example, when commenting on social media, students should use respectful language even when they disagree with others. Online bullying is not acceptable behavior.

Class activity:
Students will role-play different online scenarios and demonstrate good netiquette.

Evaluation questions:
What is cyber ethics?
Name two rules of good netiquette.
Give an example of disrespectful online behavior.

Summary:
Good behavior online helps create a safe and respectful internet environment.

topics.title: MID-TERM BREAK
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and prepare for the next term

Introduction:
This week is a break from school work.

Content:
Students will have time to rest and recharge for the next term of learning. This break helps students stay healthy and ready to learn more about digital technologies when they return.

Class activity:
No formal class activities this week.

Evaluation questions:
No evaluation questions during break week.

Summary:
Enjoy the break and come back ready to learn more about digital technologies.

topics.title: Online Privacy and Protection
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the importance of online privacy
The students should be able to identify methods of protecting personal data
The students should be able to explain how to avoid digital theft

Introduction:
Last term we learned about internet safety and security. Today we will focus on how to protect our personal information online.

Content:
Online privacy means keeping your personal information safe when using the internet. Personal data includes your name, address, phone number and bank details. In Nigeria, this is important when using mobile money like M-Pesa or when shopping online with your ATM card. Digital theft happens when hackers steal your information to use it without permission. To protect yourself, use strong passwords with numbers and letters, avoid sharing passwords with friends, and be careful when using public Wi-Fi at places like computer villages or cybercafes.

Class activity:
Students will create a poster showing three ways to protect their personal information online.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is online privacy?
2. List two types of personal data that should be protected online.
3. Why is it dangerous to use the same password for many accounts?
4. How can you protect yourself from digital theft?

Summary:
Protecting your personal information online is very important to prevent theft and keep your data safe.

topics.title: Managing Digital Footprint
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define digital footprint
The students should be able to explain the importance of managing digital footprint
The students should be able to suggest ways to create a positive online presence

Introduction:
We have learned about online privacy and protection. Today we will discuss how our online actions create a digital footprint that can affect our future.

Content:
A digital footprint is the trail of data we leave behind when we use the internet. This includes comments, photos, and searches. In Nigeria, universities and employers may check your digital footprint when you apply for admission or jobs. A positive digital footprint shows you as responsible and professional. For example, sharing educational content about Nigerian culture or helping classmates with schoolwork online creates a good footprint. To maintain a positive footprint, think before you post, avoid sharing inappropriate photos, and use respectful language in comments, just like you would when talking to someone face-to-face in the market.

Class activity:
Students will analyze their own social media profiles and suggest three improvements to create a more positive digital footprint.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is a digital footprint?
2. Why is managing your digital footprint important for your future?
3. Give one example of a positive online action.
4. How can your digital footprint affect your job opportunities in Nigeria?

Summary:
Your digital footprint represents your online reputation and can impact your future opportunities.

topics.title: Digital Project: Online Business Simulation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create a mock e-business plan
The students should be able to design a simple blog or website
The students should be able to explain basic online business concepts

Introduction:
We have learned about online privacy and digital footprints. Now we will apply this knowledge by creating our own online business.

Content:
An online business is a company that operates on the internet instead of having a physical shop. In Nigeria, many businesses like Jumia or Konga started this way. For this project, you can create a mock e-business selling local products like beads, fabrics, or agricultural produce from your state. Alternatively, you can create a blog about Nigerian culture, education, or sports. Your business plan should include what you will sell, who your customers are, and how you will protect their data. Your blog should have at least three pages with interesting content and proper privacy settings.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create either a mock e-business website using free online tools or a blog with at least three posts about Nigerian culture.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is an online business?
2. Name two popular Nigerian e-commerce websites.
3. Why is protecting customer data important for an online business?
4. What are the main components of your business plan?

Summary:
Creating an online business helps you practice digital skills while learning about entrepreneurship in the digital age.

topics.title: REVISION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall key concepts from the term
The students should be able to answer questions about online privacy
The students should be able to explain digital footprint management
The students should be able to describe online business concepts

Introduction:
This week we will revise what we have learned this term to prepare for your examination. We will go through the main topics and answer any questions you may have.

Content:
We will review three main topics: Online Privacy and Protection, Managing Digital Footprint, and Online Business Simulation. For online privacy, we will discuss how to protect personal information and avoid digital theft. For digital footprint, we will cover what it is and how to create a positive online presence. For the online business project, we will recap the key components of creating a mock e-business or blog. We will use examples relevant to Nigerian contexts, such as protecting M-Pesa transactions or creating a blog about Nigerian culture.

Class activity:
Students will work in teams to create mind maps of the three main topics, including examples and key points for each.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is online privacy important in Nigeria?
2. How does your digital footprint affect your future?
3. What are three things to consider when creating an online business?
4. How can you protect customer data in an online business?

Summary:
Revision helps reinforce what we have learned and prepares us for the examination.

topics.title: EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate understanding of digital technologies concepts
The students should be able to apply knowledge to solve problems
The students should be able to communicate ideas clearly about digital topics

Introduction:
Today you will write your end of term examination. This will test your knowledge of the digital technologies topics we have covered this term.

Content:
The examination will cover all topics from this term, including Online Privacy and Protection, Managing Digital Footprint, and Online Business Simulation. You will answer multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions. For example, you may need to explain how to protect personal information online, describe how to create a positive digital footprint, or outline a plan for an online business selling Nigerian products. Remember to read each question carefully before answering and manage your time wisely.

Class activity:
Students will write the examination paper within the allocated time.

Evaluation questions:
The examination paper will contain various questions testing recall, understanding, and application of the term's content.

Summary:
The examination assesses your understanding of digital technologies concepts learned this term.

topics.title: CLOSING/VACATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning this term
The students should be able to set goals for digital technology skills improvement

Introduction:
As we conclude this term, let's reflect on what we have learned about digital technologies and how we can continue to improve our skills.

Content:
This term we have learned about online privacy, digital footprint management, and online business concepts. These skills are important in our increasingly digital world. During the vacation, you can practice these skills by helping your family with online security, creating positive content on social media, or even starting a small online project about Nigerian culture. Remember to continue learning about new digital technologies and how to use them responsibly and safely.

Class activity:
Students will write one paragraph about what they learned this term and one goal they have for improving their digital skills next term.

Evaluation questions:
1. What was the most important thing you learned this term?
2. How will you apply your digital skills during the vacation?
3. What digital skill would you like to learn next term?

Summary:
This term has equipped us with valuable digital skills that we can continue to develop during the vacation and beyond.
